phrases.latin: Tum Theodōrus patrem quaeritāre coepit: «Ubi es, tata?» «Ecce mē.»
phrases.english: Then Theo started looking for Dad: “Where are you, Dad?” “Here I am.”
phrases.source: Libellus II, Sintra: castellum et puteus

phrases.latin: Theodōrus, post sellās latēns, clāmitābat: «Quaere mē, tata!»
phrases.english: Theo, hiding behind the seats, kept calling, “Find me, Dad!”
phrases.source: Libellus VI, Reditus: per Alpēs domum

sources: Lewis & Short: latito · Lewis & Short: quaerito
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 52, checked against the searchable text of the book (29 October 2026).

Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
